Hinge Romance Scam UK: Warning Signs and What to Do

A request for money, vouchers, cryptocurrency or an investment from someone you know only online is the decisive warning sign — however convincing the profile feels.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-07-14 · Updated 2026-07-30 · 4 min read

Quick answer: However genuine a Hinge match feels, a request for money, vouchers, cryptocurrency or an investment from someone you know only online is the decisive warning sign of romance fraud. Do not pay; report the profile through Hinge's three-dot menu, and if you have sent money, contact your bank immediately and ask it to assess an APP reimbursement claim.
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

What is a Hinge romance scam?

Romance fraud is a deliberately fabricated relationship used to gain trust and exploit someone financially. On Hinge, a criminal may use a false or stolen identity, build contact over time and then introduce an emergency, travel cost, investment or other reason to send money.

A profile can also belong to a real person whose photos or account have been misused. The important test is the behaviour and the payment request, not whether the profile initially looks authentic.

Warning signs

  • They ask for money, vouchers, cryptocurrency, financial details or an investment.
  • The request is urgent or secret, or they discourage you from discussing the relationship with friends and family.
  • They quickly try to move the conversation away from Hinge. Hinge warns that people with bad intentions may do this to get away from its message filters and reporting tools.
  • They repeatedly avoid meeting, a phone call or a video call. This is an indicator, not proof by itself.
  • Their identity, location or personal story is inconsistent.
  • A supposed emergency, journey home, business problem or investment appears only after trust has been established.

Hinge's own safety advice says to report a user who asks for money.

How the manipulation develops

The contact may feel attentive and personal because the criminal is deliberately learning what matters to the person they are targeting. UK fraud-reporting guidance says romance fraud can continue for months or years and may isolate the victim from people who could challenge the story.

The first request may be small. Later requests can be framed as proof of commitment, a loan, an emergency or access to an investment. A second payment does not recover the first. Criminals may also return later pretending that they can recover the loss for a fee.

Useful checks — and their limits

Run a reverse-image search to see whether profile photos appear under another identity. Ask questions, take time and speak to someone you trust before making any financial decision. Keeping the conversation in Hinge while you assess the match also preserves its reporting route.

No single online check proves that a person is genuine. A clean image search proves only that the tool found no match. Social accounts can be fabricated or compromised, and a phone or video call does not validate every claim. Never send money, vouchers, cryptocurrency or investment funds to someone you know only online.

If you sent money

Stop further payments and contact the bank or payment provider immediately through its official app, website or the number on your card. Describe it as a scam and ask about recall and reimbursement. Preserve the profile, messages, payment details and any account or wallet identifiers before blocking and reporting the contact.

The Payment Systems Regulator says romance scams can fall within the mandatory APP reimbursement protections for qualifying UK Faster Payments and CHAPS transfers. Coverage depends on the payment, account and scheme rules, so ask the bank to assess the claim rather than assuming the loss is final. Card, cash, gift-card, international-transfer and cryptocurrency payments follow different recovery processes; contact the relevant provider urgently.

Report the account and the fraud

Hinge says a profile or chat can be reported through the three-dot menu and that reports are confidential. If the profile is no longer visible, use Hinge's Safety and Reporting support route; its Past Matches reporting feature is not available to every user.

Report financial loss to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland. In Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101. Forward a suspicious SMS text to 7726 so the mobile provider can investigate it. Forward a suspicious email to report@phishing.gov.uk; this reports the message to the NCSC but does not replace a fraud report.

Frequently asked questions

Does moving a conversation away from Hinge prove it is a scam?

No. It is a warning sign rather than proof. Hinge says users with bad intentions often try to move conversations away quickly, so slow down and do not send money or financial information.

Can a video call or established social account prove the match is genuine?

No. These checks may reveal inconsistencies, but they cannot authenticate every claim or payment request. Treat any request for money, vouchers, cryptocurrency or an investment as unsafe.

Can my bank reimburse a romance-scam transfer?

Possibly. The mandatory APP rules can cover romance scams involving qualifying UK Faster Payments or CHAPS transfers. Contact the bank immediately and ask it to assess the claim under the current reimbursement rules; other payment methods have different protections.

How do I report someone who has unmatched me?

Where Hinge's Past Matches feature is available, it may show matches from the previous 30 days and provide a Report option. Because Hinge describes this as a limited test, use its Safety and Reporting support form if the feature is unavailable.

Should I send a small amount to test whether the story is genuine?

No. A small first payment can be used to make later requests feel easier. Do not send more money to recover an earlier payment or pay anyone who promises to recover a loss for an upfront fee.

Fast checks

  • Pause before sending money or credentials
  • Verify with an official site, app, or number
  • Never share one-time passcodes
  • Be sceptical of bank transfer pressure
